resolutions.title: The contract's flag entries and the validator's split rule are underspecified on value arity and short aliases, and two swept snippets need both to validate.
resolutions.action: D1 now specifies the flag entry shape `{ long, short, takes_value }` derived from the FLAGS / INHERITED FLAGS line grammar (`-q, --jq expression` → alias + takes a value; `--draft` with no TYPE → boolean), names the two existing snippets that require it, and D3's tokenizer consumes it (a value-taking flag eats the next token or its `=value`; a boolean eats nothing). Task 1.1 parses the entries; 1.2 hand-checks `--draft` and `-q`; 2.1 consumes them and unit-tests both snippets accepted.

resolutions.title: The `--version` command entry contradicts the freshness assertion: `gh --version --help` prints the version banner, so that entry has no usage line and no flags.
resolutions.action: Option A, settled under R-crc-3 (Sal's standing chat delegation of method, 2026-09-11). `--version` is no longer a command entry: the contract carries a top-level `availability_probe: { argv, stdout }` beside `gh_version`; the command set is the SEVEN commands the references invoke; the stub answers the probe from the captured stdout; the freshness test asserts the probe exists and every one of the seven commands has a usage line and ≥ 1 flag entry. Task 1.1/1.2/1.3 and 2.2/2.3 aligned; D1 and D3 (probe matched first in lookup) updated.
resolutions.resolution: A — the probe is a top-level contract entry, not a command; it has no help page to parse.
